note: Ratchet for `scripts/loc-metrics.py`. Every number below is lines of git-tracked source, classified by the lexer in `scripts/lib/loc_classify.py`. They may only go DOWN — raising a limit to make a build green defeats the point of measuring, so a rise fails the gate. When a rise is deliberate, run `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline` and commit the new file in the SAME commit that grew the tree. Generated files (`@generated` / `DO NOT EDIT` in the header) are measured but excluded from these limits, because appending a wire kind must never fail a size gate. The `*.comment` numbers are measured and diffed but NOT gated: a gate that makes deleting documentation the cheapest way to go green is pointed at the wrong thing. What these limits do NOT cover, stated so the total has a denominator: the programme's own tooling, 11 `.py` files (3,434 code lines) and 25 `.sh` files (3,821), 7,255 code lines in all -- roughly 4.4% of the tree, and rising, because this tooling is inside its own blind spot. Counting them needs a `#`-comment lexer for two more languages, here-documents and docstrings included, and until that exists moving logic into a script still reads as reduction.

--- PR #222 wave, verbatim ---

2026-08-10 on the MERGED PR #222 review-wave tree, after the round-4 corrections, by `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline`. Read this field before assuming a rise was lazy.

The total reads 163,653 against the 159,400 this branch carried before the wave, and **4,033 of that 4,253 is not growth**: it is Kotlin entering the gate for the first time (`kotlin.main.code` 4,012 + `kotlin.test.code` 21 -- the Android front end, `build-logic`, and every `build.gradle.kts`). Measure `main` with this same lexer and it reads 173,114, not the 169,094 the pre-Kotlin tool reported, so the programme's like-for-like result is 173,114 -> 163,653 = -9,461, -5.47%. Quoting a delta against a total from a different lexer compares two different questions.

The Rust movement includes a +54/-54 correction between the two Rust buckets, not a change to the tree: `#[cfg(test)] mod test_support;` is an unbraced item, and `_block_end` used to run past it to the next depth-0 brace, so the entire body of `async fn main()` in both the tracker and the rendezvous was counted as test code. The remainder, about +220 across the whole tree, is real and is this wave's own work: nine new Rust tests, seven new Java tests, five new lexer self-test cases and the reasons recorded beside them, netted against the Java deletions.

Every bucket sits exactly on its measured value, because that is what `--baseline` writes; there is never any headroom, so a one-line fix and its test cost a stamp. That pressure is the known cost of an exact ratchet, and the answer to it is a reason recorded here, not a limit with slack in it.
